description: For mBank S.A., pobočka zahraničnej banky (SK), sk-language searching using 'výročná správa' + 'pobočka zahraničnej banky' returned only registry and directory pages (finstat, Wikipedia, banky.sk) — no mBank.sk IR or annual-report page surfaced.

result.result_summary: No SK-side mBank annual report hub located in this pass; branch entities may report only through the Polish parent (mBank S.A. IR) and registeruz.sk.

why_it_matters: Branch-form banks are a structural blind spot: they can be materially present in SK retail while publishing nothing SK-specific.

description: OTP Banka Slovensko appears in search results only as a dissolved entity (ceased 1 Oct 2021, absorbed into ČSOB SK).

result.result_summary: Treat OTP Banka Slovensko as historical-only; its documents live in registeruz/finstat archives, not on a live IR site.

why_it_matters: Prevents wasting collection budget on a dead actor and explains discontinuities in SK market-share series around 2021.

description: For Prima banka and UniCredit Bank CZ&SK (SK site) only document PDFs surfaced, not the listing pages that link them; hub URLs recorded are inferred entry points, not observed listings.

result.result_summary: Document-level URLs are solid; hub-level URLs need a crawl pass to confirm.

why_it_matters: Collection needs a stable listing page to detect new filings — non-guessable PDF IDs make document-only knowledge unsustainable.

description: All candidates were derived from search-result metadata; no URL in this slice was fetched and none should be treated as liveness-verified.

result.result_summary: Confidence scores reflect evidence strength from search results only.

why_it_matters: Downstream verification pass must resolve every URL; 403/timeout should be read as bot-defence, not death.

description: Privatbanka, Fio banka SK branch, J&T Banka SK, Wüstenrot/ČSOB stavebná sporiteľňa and other second-tier SK institutions did not yield IR pages in the queries run.

result.result_summary: Cell coverage is strong for the seven systemic retail/universal banks, thin below them.

why_it_matters: Niche and challenger banks often reveal payments/product shifts earliest.

description: UniCredit does not operate a separate Slovak bank: the Slovak business has run since 1 December 2013 as an organisational unit (pobocka zahranicnej banky) of UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, a.s., domiciled in Prague. No standalone SK segment P&L was found at either the Prague entity or UniCredit Group level.

result.result_summary: Only combined CZ+SK figures located (e.g. group net profit CZK 5,853m at 30 June 2024); no SK-only split found in the reports reached.

why_it_matters: Any 'Slovakia' market share or profitability series built from parent disclosures will have a structural hole for UniCredit; SK-only UniCredit figures must come from NBS aggregate statistics or the SK organisational unit's local filings instead.

description: J&T Finance Group SE and PPF are privately held and run no conventional investor-relations site with quarterly presentations; disclosure is limited to annual (and for J&T, semi-annual) statutory/bond-issuer reports plus press releases, largely in Czech/Slovak.

result.result_summary: Found consolidated annual reports (JTFG SE 2024 PDF; PPF Group annual accounts 2022/2024/2025) but no quarterly segment reporting, no results presentations, no fact books.

why_it_matters: The domestically-controlled part of the SK banking market (J&T Banka SK, 365.bank, Postova banka; Home Credit SK) will be observable only at annual frequency and with far less granularity than Erste/KBC/RBI/Intesa units — a permanent asymmetry in any quarterly SK market model.

description: Slovak-language searching for the parent-IR channel itself (queries using 'materska skupina', 'prezentacia pre investorov', 'segment Slovensko', 'stvrtrocne vysledky') returned almost no parent-published Slovak material.

result.result_summary: SK queries surfaced subsidiary annual reports, SK/CZ trade press and aggregators (finstat.sk, teraz.sk, patria.cz, e15.cz, kurzy.cz) rather than parent IR pages. Parents publish this channel in English (and German/Italian/Dutch), not Slovak.

why_it_matters: Confirms a structural rule for this cell: local-language crawling is the wrong instrument for parent IR. SK terms are still essential for the subsidiary mirrors and for SK/CZ media that relay parent numbers, so both language tracks must be kept but pointed at different targets.

description: Several parents serve report files from cache-busting or hashed CDN paths that cannot be templated: KBC (wcmassets.kbc.be/.../<file>.pdf.cdn.res/last-modified/<epoch>/<file>.pdf), RBI (*.coredownload.pdf/.xlsm), PPF (datocms-assets.com/<id>/<epoch>-<name>.pdf), J&T (kc-usercontent.com GUID paths).

result.result_summary: Direct file URLs observed in search results, but each embeds a timestamp or GUID that changes on republication.

why_it_matters: A collector that hardcodes these URLs will silently rot. Link resolution must always start from the HTML index page, and stored URLs should be treated as snapshots, not durable identifiers.

description: No URL in this slice is claimed as verified-live. Only three pages were actually fetched in this pass (Erste financial-reports index, RBI reports page, Intesa subsidiaries-annual-reports page); all others come from search-result metadata.

result.result_summary: Three successful fetches, zero observed 403/404/timeouts.

why_it_matters: Liveness, robots/ToS posture and bot-defence behaviour for the remaining domains (kbc.com, group.intesasanpaolo.com deep PDFs, ppf.eu, jtbanka.sk, unicreditbank.cz/sk, ftp.pse.cz, finstat.sk) are unverified hypotheses for the deterministic verification pass.

description: Attempt to fetch https://www.trend.sk/financie failed with a tool-level refusal ('unable to fetch from www.trend.sk').

result.result_summary: No page content obtained; section structure, paywall behaviour and RSS availability for TREND remain unknown. Recorded as unverified, NOT dead — a single refused fetch is consistent with bot defence or a fetch-tool domain restriction.

why_it_matters: TREND is one of the two flagship named outlets for this cell; leaving it unverified is the largest single gap in coverage of Slovak business-press earnings commentary.

description: A sk-language search explicitly naming hnonline.sk plus banking-results terms ('hnonline.sk finweb banky zisk hospodárske výsledky') returned no hnonline.sk URLs at all.

result.result_summary: The HN/Finweb section path and paywall model could not be confirmed from search. The hnonline.sk/finweb URL recorded in the candidate is inferred, not observed.

why_it_matters: Hospodárske noviny is the Slovak business daily of record; if it is genuinely poorly indexed by this search backend, the monitoring plan must rely on a direct section crawl rather than search-based discovery.

description: Two sk-language searches targeting Živé.sk payments/banking coverage ('Živé.sk platby banka novinka mobilná aplikácia' and 'zive.sk bankovníctvo platby QR platba banky Slovensko článok') returned app-store and unrelated commercial pages, no zive.sk articles.

result.result_summary: No Živé.sk article URLs or section paths were observed; the tech-media payments channel for this cell remains undocumented at URL level. One of the searches did, however, surface that a Slovak QR-payment scheme currently involves Slovenská sporiteľňa and Tatra banka with VÚB, ČSOB and Prima banka expected to join.

why_it_matters: Payments-rail news (instant payments, QR schemes, wallet launches) is not covered by the financial press; without Živé.sk (or Touchit/DSL.sk equivalents) verified, the payments half of sector=both is thinly sourced in this cell.

description: Finsider.sk was fetched successfully but no RSS/Atom feed link appeared in the rendered page.

result.result_summary: Collection for Finsider will likely need HTML section-listing crawling rather than feed subscription, unless a feed exists at an unlinked conventional path (/feed/, /rss/) — untested.

why_it_matters: Feedless collection is more brittle and more likely to trip rate limits or ToS concerns than feed polling.

description: Denník E is a paid product and most of its bank-profitability analysis (including the 'Graf dňa' series) sits behind a subscription.

result.result_summary: Article URLs and headlines are discoverable, bodies are not freely readable.

why_it_matters: The most analytical Slovak commentary on bank profitability and on the proposed transaction tax is subscription-gated; budget for a licence or accept headline-only monitoring.

description: An English-language search for Slovak bank results media coverage surfaced no dedicated English-language Slovak business outlet in this cell's results; all substantive earnings coverage found was Slovak-language.

result.result_summary: No English equivalent of Trend/HN/Finsider was identified for Slovak bank earnings. The Slovak Spectator was not confirmed by any query run here and is therefore not recorded as a candidate.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: the Slovak-language press is the only practical channel for numbers from banks that issue no English release, so sk-language collection is mandatory rather than optional.

description: No evidence found of a Fitch Ratings public rating on Tatra banka; search results indicated Fitch does not rate that issuer, and no 2025 Fitch action on Slovenská sporiteľňa surfaced.

result.result_summary: Fitch coverage of SK banks appears thinner than Moody's/S&P; Fitch is mainly a sovereign-rating source for SK.

why_it_matters: Avoids wasted collection effort building a Fitch-per-bank crawler; sets expectation that bank-level coverage is Moody's/S&P-centric.

description: ECB Supervisory Banking Statistics reports state there are no significant institutions at the highest level of consolidation in Slovakia, so SK banks are consolidated into their foreign parents (Erste, Intesa, RBI, KBC, UniCredit).

result.result_summary: SSM country tables give limited standalone SK bank-level detail.

why_it_matters: SK subsidiary-level analyst validation must come from EBA transparency data, NBS, registeruz filings and parent-group segment reporting rather than SSM aggregates.

description: Slovak-language queries for Big Four banking-sector studies returned mostly service/marketing pages and a Czech-language Deloitte press release, not SK-specific published banking surveys.

result.result_summary: Big Four SK-market banking research appears to be published regionally (CE/CEE) in English rather than as standalone Slovak-language studies.

why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring of Big Four should focus on press rooms and short commentary; the substantive numbers arrive via CE/CEE English reports.

description: No Scope Ratings coverage of Slovak banks was surfaced by the searches performed; only S&P BICRA material was found for the country-risk angle.

result.result_summary: Scope's SK bank coverage unconfirmed — treat as unverified, not absent.

why_it_matters: A smaller EU-registered agency could be a cheaper alternative source; needs a dedicated targeted check on scoperatings.com.

description: Substantive rating-agency credit opinions (Moody's, S&P) and most Big Four full reports sit behind subscriptions or registration forms; only headline ratings, rating-action press releases and regulatory disclosures are freely readable.

result.result_summary: Free layer = headline ratings + action releases; paid layer = the analytical detail.

why_it_matters: Budget and licensing decisions are needed if the programme wants the restated asset-quality/capital detail this cell is meant to deliver.

description: SZRB has no separate English investor-relations section comparable to a listed bank; disclosures observed are Slovak-first. EXIMBANKA SR is the exception, publishing bilingual sk/en annual reports and an /en/ document tree.

result.result_summary: English-only searching would surface EXIMBANKA PDFs but would largely miss SZRB, SIH and Slovenská konsolidačná disclosures.

why_it_matters: Confirms local-language collection is mandatory for this cell; an English-only pipeline would under-cover the state-owned perimeter.

description: rokovania.gov.sk serves document attachments through opaque endpoints (download.dat?id=<GUID pair>) and negotiation ids (/RVL/Negotiation/<n>) rather than stable per-report URLs; older material sits on separate subdomains (hsr.rokovania.sk, lrv.rokovania.sk).

result.result_summary: No stable, guessable permalink scheme for tabled sector reports was identified from search results.

why_it_matters: A collector must resolve agenda pages first and cannot rely on deep-linking; link rot risk is high, so attachments should be mirrored on capture.

description: MH Invest s.r.o., MH Investment s.r.o., MH Manažment and Slovenský investičný holding s.r.o. are distinct entities easily confused with Slovak Investment Holding, a. s. (formerly SZRB Asset Management); several are industrial-park/asset vehicles under the Ministry of Economy rather than financial-sector actors.

result.result_summary: Search on 'MH Invest' returns at least four different IČO-level entities; only Slovak Investment Holding a.s. is squarely in scope for banking/payments intelligence.

why_it_matters: Naive name-based collection would ingest irrelevant industrial-park financials; collection must be keyed on IČO, not name.

description: All URLs in this slice were obtained from search-result metadata; no fetch was performed to confirm reachability or current content.

result.result_summary: URLs are provided with confidence scores only.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must confirm liveness; treat any 403/timeout as bot defence rather than a dead source.

description: No Diebold Nixdorf press release naming a Slovak bank contract was found in this pass (searched EN vendor IR feed, PR Newswire and ATM Marketplace hubs).

result.result_summary: Only non-SK deals surfaced (Geldmaat NL, FOREX Nordics, awards releases). Absence is unconfirmed — the IR archive was not exhaustively paged.

why_it_matters: Diebold Nixdorf is a plausible incumbent in SK branch automation; if it never announces SK wins, the indirect route for that vendor is weak and other proxies (register filings, CRZ, job ads) must carry the load.

description: No card-personalisation bureau serving Slovak banks was publicly identified (Thales/Gemalto, IDEMIA, Giesecke+Devrient country pages did not surface with SK bank customer names).

result.result_summary: SK-language search on 'personalizácia kariet' / 'výroba platobných kariet' returned consumer-facing bank pages and glossaries, not supplier disclosures.

why_it_matters: Card personalisation is a recurring, contracted spend; without a named bureau, this sub-segment of the cell has no source coverage at all.

description: Slovak-language terminology for vendor case studies is thin: 'prípadová štúdia' is rarely used by SK IT vendors, who publish 'referencie' lists without narrative detail, and many vendor sites publish only EN case studies.

result.result_summary: SK searches returned reference index pages rather than detailed, dated deal descriptions.

why_it_matters: Collection design must expect low-signal reference lists and rely on diffing lists over time plus EN-language vendor case studies for narrative.

description: Several candidate URLs (Softec, Ingenico newsroom, NCR Atleos news index, ce.asseco.com annual report PDF) were identified via search results rather than fetched in this pass.

result.result_summary: URLs recorded with confidence scores; liveness left to the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Prevents recording bot-defended or moved pages as dead sources.

description: No EDGAR-style single full-text, machine-readable filing archive exists for Slovak banks. Disclosure is split between RÚZ (accounting statements), CERI (regulated information from securities issuers) and issuers' own IR pages; none offers EDGAR-like full-text search across all filings.

result.result_summary: Searched sk and en for a consolidated SK filing search engine; found only the three separate silos plus commercial aggregators.

why_it_matters: Any time-series build must join at least RÚZ + CERI + issuer sites on IČO/LEI; budget for reconciliation rather than expecting one archive.

description: Could not confirm an active 'Cribis Universal Register' product offered for Slovakia by Dun & Bradstreet/Bisnode; search returned only the Bisnode→D&B Slovakia rename (effective 2022) and generic D&B products.

result.result_summary: No SK Cribis landing page surfaced in either language.

why_it_matters: Avoids recording a non-existent SK product line; the CRIF/Cribis family may cover SK under a different brand and needs a dedicated check.

description: The OpenCorporates Slovakia jurisdiction URL was inferred from the platform's standard URL pattern rather than confirmed in search results, and no bulk SK export offer was found.

result.result_summary: English query returned only generic OpenCorporates commentary about indexing the SK commercial register.

why_it_matters: Treat that candidate's URL and bulk availability as unverified until the deterministic liveness pass runs.

description: No established Slovak-language term was found for 'machine-readable mirror' or 'bulk download archive' as a category; practitioners use borrowed English ('SQL dump', 'API', 'dataset') inside Slovak sentences.

result.result_summary: Local-language searching had to rely on 'otvorené dáta', 'hromadné stiahnutie' and English-in-Slovak terms.

why_it_matters: Future query expansion for this cell should mix Slovak nouns with English technical tokens rather than seeking pure-Slovak equivalents.

description: No dedicated Slovak POS/acquiring/terminal industry conference was found. sk queries on payments conferences returned general fintech/banking events (Finweek, FinNext, ITAPA) rather than an acceptance/terminal-specific venue.

result.result_summary: Payments-hardware and acquiring topics appear only as sessions inside broader conferences, not as standalone SK events.

why_it_matters: Acceptance-side milestones (terminal counts, softPOS, eKasa integration) must be harvested from session-level programmes rather than from a single dedicated venue - raises collection cost and the chance of missing a signal.

description: LinkedIn - the seed query's named channel for CEO/bank milestone announcements - is login-walled and its ToS restricts automated collection. Search returned only company/profile landing pages, no post-level content.

result.result_summary: Individual milestone posts could not be enumerated from open search; only the company page URL and secondary reporting of post content were obtainable.

why_it_matters: A core surface of this cell (executive communication) cannot be collected automatically without a licensed feed; the routine must plan for manual monitoring or accept lag via press-room mirrors.

description: No page was fetched directly in this pass; all candidate URLs come from search-result metadata and snippets. Liveness, robots.txt posture and paywall status are therefore hypotheses, not verdicts.

result.result_summary: All URLs recorded unverified by design; deterministic liveness pass required.

why_it_matters: Downstream collectors must not assume any URL here is reachable; a 403 on e.g. mastercard.com or forbes.sk should be read as bot-defence, not as a dead source.

description: Two apparently distinct Slovak fintech association web presences were found - finas.sk (FINAS, active meetups, awards, expansion hub) and slovakfintech.sk (eventy/novinky, Open Banking platform). Their relationship (rename, split, or two bodies) was not resolved.

result.result_summary: Both listed as separate candidates pending clarification.

why_it_matters: Risk of double-counting the same association's events, or of dropping the still-active one if they are merged incorrectly.

description: No established Slovak-language term was identified for 'earnings call' / 'investor day' in the SK bank context - SK banks are largely subsidiaries of foreign groups (Erste, Intesa, RBI, KBC) and do not hold local earnings calls, so the spoken-disclosure channel is conferences and awards rather than IR events.

result.result_summary: sk queries for executive result presentations returned conference and award content, not IR calls.

why_it_matters: Confirms the premise of this cell: for SK, group-level IR (Vienna/Milan/Brussels) plus local conference/award stages together substitute for a domestic earnings-call channel; the routine should also watch parent-group IR.

description: Searched in Slovak for an open dataset or API exposing the Zbierka listín (commercial register document collection) itself. data.gov.sk and the MS SR open-data page point to register APIs (RPVS, ress-isu Swagger) but no evidence was found of a bulk, machine-readable feed of the scanned listiny.

result.result_summary: Document lists appear reachable per-entity via orsr.sk zbl.asp; full documents are requested via sluzby.orsr.sk, seemingly with eID and/or a court fee.

why_it_matters: Corporate-action monitoring for non-listed SK banks/PSPs will need per-entity polling rather than a bulk feed, which raises collection cost and argues for prioritising a watchlist.

description: No official English-language interface was found for registeruz.sk or orsr.sk; English search results consistently redirect to commercial intermediaries (FinStat English services, Schmidt & Schmidt) or the EU BRIS node.

result.result_summary: English-only collection of the SK statutory channel is not viable; Slovak-language parsing of form templates and document labels is required.

why_it_matters: Downstream extraction must handle Slovak field names (súvaha, výkaz ziskov a strát, poznámky, správa audítora); budget for a Slovak term mapping layer.

description: The domain registeructovnychzavierok.sk closely mimics the official registeruz.sk but is a private explainer site, not the statutory register.

result.result_summary: Recorded as low-credibility context source; official register is registeruz.sk (MF SR / DataCentrum).

why_it_matters: Prevents a collector or analyst from citing a non-authoritative site as the statutory source.

description: Several URLs recorded here (rpvs.gov.sk root, api.statistics.sk/rpo/v1/, sluzby.orsr.sk, the Slovensko.Digital S3 dump link) were referenced by search results or documentation pages but not individually fetched in this pass.

result.result_summary: Recorded with URL + confidence only; no liveness claim made, per run rules.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should prioritise these before a collector is built against them.

description: Searched in Slovak for a dedicated statutory filing channel specific to platobné inštitúcie / inštitúcie elektronických peňazí (separate from the generic RÚZ). None was found; NBS registers list authorisations but appear not to host the entities' own financial statements.

result.result_summary: Payment-institution accounts must be sourced from the generic RÚZ, keyed by IČO obtained from NBS lists.

why_it_matters: Confirms the pointer→direct chain (NBS actor list → RPO IČO → RÚZ filings) as the correct architecture for this cell.

description: Searched CERI's own documentation pages (/docs, /categories, /manuals) for an API, RSS feed, bulk export or open-data dump of regulated information. None is documented: the site advertises only a database search UI with print/download of individual documents.

result.result_summary: No API/RSS/bulk-download endpoint found for ceri.nbs.sk. Collection will require HTML crawling of the search interface plus per-document file retrieval.

why_it_matters: Sets the engineering cost and fragility of the single most important source in this cell, and strengthens the case for planning a migration to ESAP structured access from 2027.

description: Every direct WebFetch attempt against www.bsse.sk returned 'connect ECONNREFUSED 195.80.190.46:443'. Search engines index the same URLs and PDFs hosted on bsse.sk appear in results, so the site is very likely live.

result.result_summary: bsse.sk not fetchable from this environment; treated as bot-defended/geo-restricted, NOT dead. Content for BCPB candidates was reconstructed from search-result metadata and NBS descriptions rather than direct reading.

why_it_matters: The exchange is a core node of this cell. If the block is IP-based, the deterministic verification pass and the eventual collector must run from an EU egress or via a headless browser; otherwise the whole BCPB branch will be falsely marked dead.

description: Searched in both Slovak and English for a public, per-bank MREL/resolution disclosure register for Slovakia (e.g. a Rada pre riešenie krízových situácií / resolution council publication of bank-level MREL targets or eligible-liability issuance). No such Slovak national register surfaced within this run.

result.result_summary: No SK-specific public MREL disclosure store identified; MREL-eligible senior instruments appear only indirectly via issuer prospectuses and CERI filings.

why_it_matters: MREL issuance is one of the stated triggers for this cell's regulated-disclosure flow; without a dedicated register, MREL intelligence must be reconstructed from prospectuses, Pillar 3 reports and parent-group disclosures, which is slower and less complete.

description: Slovak-language searching for foreign-venue listings of Slovak bank instruments (e.g. covered bonds or senior notes listed in Luxembourg or Vienna rather than on BCPB) produced no clear local-language term or index. Slovak terminology exists for the instruments (kryté dlhopisy, hypotekárne záložné listy) but not for a 'foreign listing venue' concept that search engines resolve.

result.result_summary: Could not establish, in this run, whether and where SK bank benchmark covered bonds are listed outside BCPB.

why_it_matters: If benchmark issues are listed abroad, the SK regulated-disclosure channel (CERI/BCPB) would be incomplete for the largest transactions, and the collection plan would need a foreign-OAM branch.

description: CERI documentation states that filings submitted before 31 July 2011 may require in-person consultation at NBS headquarters by appointment, even though electronic storage nominally begins 1 June 2007.

result.result_summary: Pre-2011 regulated information is only partially available online.

why_it_matters: Caps the depth of any automated long-run time series for SK bank disclosure at roughly 2011 without manual archival work.

description: The Slovak phrase 'Pilier 3' / '3. pilier' is heavily overloaded. It most commonly means the third pension pillar (doplnkové dôchodkové sporenie) in consumer-facing content, and secondarily the Solvency II insurance Pillar III. Banking CRR Pillar 3 results were repeatedly crowded out by pension articles (podnikajte.sk, banky.sk).

result.result_summary: Effective SK queries must avoid bare 'Pilier 3' and instead use 'opatrenie NBS č. 16/2014', 'uverejňovanie informácií bankami', 'informácie o banke k <date>', or 'informácie o činnosti banky'.

why_it_matters: A naive SK keyword collector on 'Pilier 3' will return mostly pension-product marketing and near-zero prudential disclosure, silently producing a false coverage gap.

description: No official standalone website for Garančný fond investícií (Investment Guarantee Fund) was located in this pass, despite it being an NBS-supervised statutory body under Act 566/2001 §80 with an annual-reporting obligation. Only third-party descriptions (fio.sk PDF, fininfo.sk, finstat.sk) surfaced.

result.result_summary: GFI recorded as a lower-confidence candidate pointing at secondary sources; its primary domain remains unidentified.

why_it_matters: GFI is the investor-protection counterpart to FOV and belongs in the same compelled-disclosure family; leaving its primary channel unmapped is a real hole in this cell.

description: The Rezolučná rada's 'Vybrané právoplatné rozhodnutia' page appears to contain no published decisions to date.

result.result_summary: Recorded as a source to monitor rather than as a data source, since a first entry would be a high-signal resolution event.

why_it_matters: Distinguishing 'channel exists but is empty' from 'channel does not exist' matters — the former is a live tripwire, the latter is a gap. This is the former.

description: SRB MREL dashboards are aggregate across the SRB remit; no SK-country or SK-bank-level MREL breakdown was found in the dashboard publications, and no Slovakia-specific MREL disclosure list was found on srb.europa.eu.

result.result_summary: Bank-level MREL for SK institutions must be sourced from each bank's own Pillar 3 / MREL disclosure, not from the SRB dashboard.

why_it_matters: Prevents an incorrect collection design that expects country-level MREL series from the SRB.

description: No dedicated disclosure landing pages were located this pass for Privatbanka, a.s., Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka, a.s. (SZRB), UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia (SK branch), or Wüstenrot stavebná sporiteľňa, despite all of them being subject to Opatrenie 16/2014.

result.result_summary: Absent from the candidate list; requires a targeted per-domain navigation pass rather than keyword search.

why_it_matters: Smaller and state-owned institutions have thin SEO footprints; keyword search systematically under-covers them, biasing the source map toward the big four.

description: No NBS page was found publishing bank-level ICAAP/ILAAP outcomes, SREP capital requirements (P2R), or O-SII/systemic-risk buffer decisions per institution, though NBS is the designated macroprudential authority and such decisions are normally published.

result.result_summary: Searched with SK macroprudential terms ('makroprudenciálna politika', 'vankúš', 'ozdravné plány') and hit only institutional/history pages.

why_it_matters: P2R and buffer decisions are a compelled, structured, bank-level supervisory disclosure stream — arguably the highest-value part of this cell — and it is currently unmapped.

description: The guessed Slovak-language NBS path https://nbs.sk/dohlad-nad-financnym-trhom/dohlad/platobne-sluzby-a-elektronicke-peniaze/platobne-institucie/ returned HTTP 404 on one fetch attempt.

result.result_summary: Only the English-language equivalents under /en/financial-market-supervision1/supervision/payment-services-and-electronic-money/ were confirmed in search results. The SK slug likely differs rather than being absent; treat as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: Slovak-language regulator pages are the preferred citation for a SK cell; the correct SK slug must be resolved from the NBS site navigation before collection is automated.

description: Targeted Slovak-language searching for press releases or investor pages of several NBS-licensed payment institutions (Payout a.s., K-PAY a.s., Ultima Payments a.s., BLIK SK, a.s.) returned no corporate newsroom.

result.result_summary: These entities surface only as register rows; no own-site disclosures located in this pass.

why_it_matters: For most SK payment institutions the ONLY reliable disclosure route is the statutory filing register (RÚZ) plus the commercial register, not company communications — collection design must assume filings-first.

description: No investor-relations function exists for the SK payments cell: no SK-domiciled payment or e-money institution was found to be listed on the Bratislava Stock Exchange or to publish IR material.

result.result_summary: Searches for investor relations / earnings material for SK PIs returned nothing; the sector is entirely privately held or foreign-parented.

why_it_matters: The workstream topics 'investor relations' and 'earnings' cannot be satisfied at SK entity level for payments; earnings signals must be taken from group-level IR of foreign parents (e.g. Global Payments Inc.) or from RÚZ filings.

description: Several local-language search terms proved noisy.

result.result_summary: 'elektronické peniaze' pulls in Ministry of Finance consumer-education pages and FIU AML reports; 'výročná správa' alone pulls government-body annual reports; the abbreviation 'SBA' collides with the banking association and unrelated bodies; 'Trust Pay' collides with 'TRUST účtovná kancelária s. r. o.'.

why_it_matters: Automated query generation for this cell must pin queries to entity IČO or to the exact licence-category phrase to avoid heavy false positives.

description: No named full inštitúcia elektronických peňazí list was retrieved directly from an NBS page in this pass; the NBS EMI page is definitional and defers to a 'List of subjects' link.

result.result_summary: SKPAY, a. s. was confirmed as a payment AND e-money institution via Slovenská pošta and its own site, but a complete SK EMI roster was not enumerated.

why_it_matters: The EMI sub-population of this cell is currently under-enumerated relative to the payment-institution sub-population.

description: No dedicated Slovak-language newsroom or press-release archive was found for Visa or Mastercard covering Slovakia. SK-relevant scheme news (e.g. Click to Pay arriving in Slovakia) was only observable via the pan-European Mastercard newsroom and via SK tech-media pickup (touchit.sk).

result.result_summary: Searches in sk and en returned only global/Europe newsrooms plus a Mastercard Slovakia Instagram account; no sk press-release index.

why_it_matters: SK scheme announcements must be caught downstream (SK media, agency tag pages) rather than at source, which adds latency and attribution risk.

description: Neither Worldline nor Nexi discloses Slovakia as a reporting unit. Worldline group FY/H1 releases name Italy, Switzerland, UK, Germany, France and Belgium but not Slovakia; Nexi reports Slovakia only inside an aggregated CSEE segment alongside Poland, Croatia, Hungary and Serbia.

result.result_summary: No SK line item found in any group-level acquirer/processor disclosure reviewed.

why_it_matters: SK acquiring/processing revenue can only be reconstructed from SK statutory filings (registeruz/ORSR), not from group investor materials - this shapes the whole collection design for cell 07.

description: Two Global Payments SK legal vehicles appear as dissolved/in liquidation in Slovak registry aggregators: 'Global Payments Europe Slovakia, s.r.o. v likvidacii' (ICO 43854958) and 'Global Payments Europe, s.r.o., organizacna zlozka' (ICO 35893630). The live vehicle appears to be 'Global Payments s.r.o., organizacna zlozka' (ICO 50010301, Vajnorska 100/B, Bratislava).

result.result_summary: Registry-aggregator listings flag [zrusena]/v likvidacii for the two older entities.

why_it_matters: Collecting against a stale ICO would silently produce empty or misleading SK financials; the entity map for this actor must be pinned to ICO 50010301 and re-checked.

description: No separate Slovak-registered Worldline legal entity was identified in this pass. Worldline appears to serve SK through worldline.com/sk-sk, a platobnyterminal.sk.worldline.com subdomain and the chcemterminal.sk channel site, suggesting cross-border/branch service rather than a SK a.s./s.r.o.

result.result_summary: Searches on 'Worldline Slovakia s.r.o.' and NBS listings returned no SK-incorporated Worldline entity.

why_it_matters: If there is no SK entity, no SK statutory accounts exist for Worldline and its SK footprint must be inferred from NBS passporting records and channel/pricing evidence instead.

description: The NBS PSD2 register API endpoint (https://subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2) and the ZBK statistics page (https://zbk.sk/statisticke-udaje/) were identified from search results but were not fetched in this pass, so their current response shape and content depth are unverified.

result.result_summary: Recorded as high-confidence candidates with unverified liveness; not treated as dead.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should prioritise these two, as both are load-bearing for the actor map and the acceptance-side time series.

description: No public source was found disclosing SK merchant-acquiring market shares (by turnover or merchant/terminal count) split between Global Payments, Worldline, Nexi and bank-owned acquirers. ZBK and SBA statistics are aggregate, not per-acquirer.

result.result_summary: Both sk and en queries returned only aggregate card statistics and vendor marketing.

why_it_matters: Any market-share view for SK acceptance will have to be modelled from statutory revenue filings plus terminal-estate proxies, not read off a published source.

description: Searched in Slovak for a standalone annual report of a SIPS operator company; SIPS has no separate operating company — it is run directly by NBS, so there is no 'prevádzkovateľ výročná správa' distinct from the NBS annual report.

result.result_summary: Only NBS pages and NBS annual reports returned; no independent clearing-house entity publishing accounts.

why_it_matters: Collection must target NBS publications rather than hunting a non-existent Slovak ACH company; avoids wasted crawl budget and false 'missing source' gaps.

description: Bankové zúčtovacie centrum Slovenska, a.s. (BZCS), the pre-2003 interbank clearing operator, was renamed RVS, a.s. and appears in the commercial register as dissolved/in liquidation.

result.result_summary: Found NBS history page and FinStat register entry; no live corporate website or ongoing disclosure.

why_it_matters: Historical clearing volumes must be sought in NBS annual reports and academic library holdings, not from the entity itself.

description: Slovak-language searching for Slovenská pošta postal payment transaction volumes (SIPO, poštový poukaz counts) returned product and tariff pages only, no published volume statistics on posta.sk.

result.result_summary: Volume data appears only, if at all, inside the annual report PDF and the RÚ universal-service report — not as a standing statistical page.

why_it_matters: Postal payment volumes will require PDF text extraction rather than a structured feed; plan parsing effort accordingly.

description: No Slovak national instant-payment scheme body separate from the EPC SEPA Instant Credit Transfer scheme was identified; NBS and SBA act as the coordinating bodies.

result.result_summary: Searches in Slovak for 'okamžité platby schéma prevádzkovateľ' returned only NBS topic pages and EPC-derived material.

why_it_matters: Instant-payment scheme intelligence for SK must come from NBS, SBA and EPC-level sources rather than a domestic scheme operator.

description: The NBS 'Prístup do platobných systémov' PDF is served from an opaque document endpoint with a force-download query parameter; it was found only via search result metadata and was not fetched.

result.result_summary: URL recorded with medium-high confidence; liveness deliberately not asserted.

why_it_matters: Deterministic verification pass should confirm; opaque GUID paths are fragile and may need re-discovery from the parent page each cycle.

description: Slovak-language searching on BNPL terms (odložená platba, platba na splátky, kúp teraz zaplať neskôr) returned almost exclusively Czech-market material (Twisto, Skip Pay, Platím Pak, Klarna, GoPay, Comgate) with only an incidental mention that Skip Pay operates in Slovakia.

result.result_summary: No SK-domiciled BNPL provider newsroom identified in this pass; SK BNPL appears to be served by CZ/EU providers rather than local actors.

why_it_matters: The BNPL leg of the cell has no confirmed local primary source, so BNPL signals for SK will have to be pulled from CZ provider newsrooms, e-shop payment-method pages and NBS consumer-credit supervision instead.

description: No dedicated Slovak fintech-only newswire or press-release distribution channel (equivalent to a national fintech PR hub) was found; SK fintech PR is dispersed across FinReport, Forbes.sk, Startitup and company sites.

result.result_summary: Searches in sk for 'tlačová správa fintech Slovensko' surfaced media articles, not a distribution platform.

why_it_matters: Collection must be multi-source and keyword-driven rather than a single feed subscription; raises the risk of missing small announcements.

description: Company homepages for Fumbi, Vacuumlabs, kevin., 365.bank and Revolut newsroom paths were inferred from coverage rather than fetched in this pass.

result.result_summary: URLs provided with reduced confidence; no liveness claim made.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve exact newsroom paths before these are wired into collection.

description: 'FINTECH SK s.r.o.' (IČO 54500923) exists as a registered SK company name, making the bare term 'fintech SK' noisy in register searches.

result.result_summary: Register lookups on the word fintech return an unrelated single company rather than the sector.

why_it_matters: Actor discovery must be driven off licence-type register queries (platobná inštitúcia, poskytovateľ služieb kryptoaktív, AISP/PISP), not name keywords.

description: No annual report (výročná správa) of the Slovak Banking Association was found published on sbaonline.sk. Fetches of the homepage, /o-nas/ and /novinka/ surfaced press releases, statistics/analyses and project pages, but no annual-report archive or downloads section.

result.result_summary: SBA appears not to self-publish an annual report; its statutory financial statements would instead sit in registeruz.sk under IČO 30813182.

why_it_matters: The workstream expects association annual reports as a direct disclosure type; for SK banking the substitute route is the state register, not the association site.

description: ALS SR site navigation (fetched) exposes members, statistics (SK/EU), documents, press releases, glossary, FAQ, videos and a vehicle register — but no annual report or publications section.

result.result_summary: Leasing association publishes recurring statistics but no annual report on its own domain.

why_it_matters: Statistics are the valuable asset here; do not budget collection effort for a non-existent report series.

description: No dedicated Slovak payment service provider / e-money institution association was found. Searches in Slovak for a payments-specific association returned only the two general fintech bodies (Slovenská FinTech asociácia, FINAS) and the e-commerce association SAEC.

result.result_summary: Payments-industry self-regulation in SK appears to be handled inside SBA's expert commissions (14 commissions, 200+ specialists, including a payments area) rather than by a standalone PSP association.

why_it_matters: Payments intelligence for SK must be sourced from SBA commissions plus the fintech associations; searching for a nonexistent SK equivalent of a payments association would waste cycles.

description: The 'bankový ombudsman SBA' — a term still widely used in SK banking glossaries — was abolished by the SBA members' assembly on 31 May 2018 and replaced from 1 July 2018 by the Inštitút alternatívneho riešenia sporov SBA.

result.result_summary: Searching 'bankový ombudsman' retrieves mostly obsolete bank-glossary pages, not a live source.

why_it_matters: A noisy legacy term; collection must target institutars.sk, and any 'bankový ombudsman' material dated after mid-2018 should be treated as stale.

description: Several association URLs were taken from the NBS directory and search results without being fetched: institutars.sk, adss.sk, adds.sk, apsu.sk, afisp.sk, aocp.sk, ass.sk, saec.sk, itas.sk/clenovia, amcham.sk, sopk.sk, asins.sk, finas.sk. Some are listed by NBS as http-only, which may indicate outdated directory entries.

result.result_summary: Recorded as candidates with confidence scores below the fetched sources; liveness left to the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Prevents overstating verification; http-only entries in a regulator directory are a common signal of redirects or moved sites, not of dead sources.

description: The NBS professional-associations directory lists the Slovak Insurance Association (SLASPO) via its ombudsman domain poistovaciombudsman.sk, and lists the asset-management association as 'www.ass.sk' while search results use the SASS branding. Canonical domains for these two bodies were not confirmed.

result.result_summary: Two association identities need a disambiguation pass before scheduled collection.

why_it_matters: Registering the wrong canonical domain would silently produce empty crawls.

description: SBA membership counts differ across its own pages: the EN about page states 29 members (25 banks), the SK about page states 24 members, and the members directory enumerates 24 (20 full + 4 associate). Sector coverage is stated as ~99% (SK) vs 100% by assets (EN).

result.result_summary: Member counts are not internally consistent; the enumerated directory is the most reliable of the three.

why_it_matters: Any headline figure quoted from SBA must cite the enumerated member list and its retrieval date, not the prose about-page numbers.
